subject: Confirming latency SLO commitment + support uplift at renewal
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: renewal conversation — SLAs and support

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the renewal heads-up. We finalize budgets early December. A couple things we need to lock before we can sign:

- A clear latency SLO for 99th percentile tail on our production routes (we’re seeing spikes when traffic bursts). We need a committed number and an escalation path.
- Confirmation that support will be upgraded to a named technical contact + 24/7 incident channel for our dedicated pool.
- Any changes in term length that affect pricing.

Could you send a short one-pager with the SLO commitment and what your on-call/incident timeline looks like under Premium? Procurement will need that for approval.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Director of Platform Engineering | Brightline Systems
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: renewal conversation — SLAs and support

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a short summary of the Premium SLA draft (redwood-premium-sla-offer-v2.pdf) and an ops runbook showing expected responses and escalation windows (throughput-latency-runbook.xlsx). High level:

- Latency SLO: 99th percentile token latency <= 450ms for the pinned production model under confirmed dedicated pool sizing.
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for the dedicated capacity plan you’re on.
- Incident response: P1 acknowledgement within 15 minutes, mitigation update within 1 hour, named TEM (Technical Engagement Manager) assigned during business hours and a 24/7 incident channel with on-call engineer.
- Remedies: credit schedule tied to sustained SLO misses (outlined in PDF).

Marissa I’ve cc’d you to confirm pricing delta for the 24/7 support add-on + case volume estimate. Grace can you confirm the ops runbook items and whether we need a short validation run (two-week canary) before the renewal commitment?

Sarah — I’m happy to hop on a short call (30m) next week to walk procurement through the doc. Proposed times: Tue 11/24 10am PT, Wed 11/25 1pm PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: renewal conversation — SLAs and support

Aditya / Sarah —

Thanks for looping me in. Pricing impact for Premium Support + 24/7 on-call is a $28K annual uplift on top of the dedicated capacity commitment. If they go to a 24-month term we can offer a 12% term discount and include the named TEM for free for the first 3 months.

Also noted: procurement will want specific language about escalation playbooks and runbook handoff. We should propose a two-week validation canary at the current committed throughput (25k tokens/min aggregate) with telemetry hooks to confirm 99th percentile latency numbers before the renewal effective date.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: renewal conversation — SLAs and support

Quick ops note —

We reviewed Brightline’s traffic profile and recommend the following before committing to the 450ms P99:

- Increase dedicated pool to +2 GPUs for peak windows or enable burst capacity (estimated cost delta included in pricing sheet).
- Enable prefix KV caching for high-frequency prompts (should reduce tail latency by ~15–25%).
- Run a 10-business-day soak at 100% expected traffic with canary routing (10% traffic to new pool, ramp to 100% on passing criteria).

I’ll prepare a concise checklist for the canary (metrics, runbook steps, rollback triggers). I propose the timeline: canary start 12/6, validation complete by 12/17, contract effective 1/1/2027 if all pass.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@brightline.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: renewal conversation — SLAs and support

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Procurement has one follow-up: can you add the specific P99 measurement method and the joint runbook acceptance criteria as a short addendum to the SLA (Procurement asks for measurable acceptance gates)? If you send that by EOD Tuesday we’ll route for legal review and aim to sign by 12/22.

Also, we accept the two-week canary timing but want a single point of contact at Brightline for communications during the run. That will be me and our SRE lead (procurement@brightline.com) on escalation lists.

If you send over the addendum + updated DocuSign link I’ll kick off legal review. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Sarah
